Considering the challenges facing the ACME Group through the increasing competitive pressure, with increasing customer and regulatory requirements, we need to continuously increase our efficiency in the Product Development Process in order to stay competitive
Looking at our current engineering practices, that are very much hardware component driven, we want to be more pro-active (up-front system design).

Furthermore, the ever increasing complexity of our products makes it necessary to always improve our current engineering practices where needed, for instance to have better control of our Product Families.
Since we have a commitment to efficiently develop and offer superior products exceeding our customers’ expectations, upfront development and Systems Engineering is a key mechanism, see Figure 1.

In this RFI, the following fields of Systems Engineering expertise will be in focus: Stakeholder Requirements Management, Requirements Management, Systems Architecture and Design (MBSE), Requirements driven Verification and Validation.
However, surrounding fields of expertise, e.g. Systems Analysis and general support processes (e.g. report & measurements, Configuration Management), is also of interest.
The next step for ACME is to start practicing Model Based Systems Engineering, MBSE.
Systems Engineering within ACME is today very requirements driven but now it is time to start looking at MBSE with support of standard general-purpose modeling language (e.g. SysML, UML and IDEF).
When describing our capabilities we have used a definition “work item”.
A work item is a single unit or object in the tool that all can build up structures or contain structures.
The different types of work items can be e.g. requirements, system elements, system structures, test cases, documents, etc.
The ACME Group has initiated a project to evaluate Systems Engineering tool sets in order to make a proposal to replace the current scattered tool environment used within the ACME Group.
The new tool set shall be used, in long term, as a global solution for the ACME Group.
The ACME Group hereby invites your company to give a proposal on a Systems Engineering tool environment according to this RFI.
Thank you for your time and diligence.
In order to propose your System Engineering tool set and to participate in our evaluation, please respond to this RFI by January 15th - 2011 at 6 pm CET.
You will then be informed whether or not you are invited to participate in following detailed evaluations.
Only responses that are 100% complete will be considered

The purpose of the present Request For Information (RFI) is to obtain preliminary proposals from all those suppliers who may be interested in providing a Communications and Information Systems architectures development tool to support the Spanish Ministry of Defense, in accordance with the criteria provided in this document.
It should be noted that the purpose of this RFI is not to obtain final proposals.
These final proposals will be the subject of a subsequent bidding process.
This RFI is not part of a contract nor does it represent a commitment to be contracted by the Spanish Ministry of Defense.
The technical information collected in this document is provided on guidance, and interested parties may include variations in such proposals information.
All information or documentation sent to the Spanish Ministry of Defense given this consultation will be confidential and will not be communicated or publicated.

The Order DEF/2639/2015, of December 3rd, which establishes the Spanish Ministry of Defense Communications and Information Systems Policy (CIS Policy), includes in its article 7 the general guidelines by which the planning and the CIS resourcing, its control, organization, operation and maintenance, for the establishment and provision of the associated services, should be governed.

Among such guidelines it is included the technical standarization of these resources, through a hierachical model of architectures similar to that used by NATO, as an instrument of coherence and technical integrity.
In the article 7.3.a), the CIS Architectures to be developed are established and organized in the following hierachical way: 1st.
Spanish Ministry of Defense Communications and Informations Systems Overarching Architecture (AG CIS/TIC);

These architectures will act as a guide and support for the structured and rigorous development of the CIS Capabilities of the Department ensuring the necessary coherence and technical integrity, the feasibility and necessary budget allocation, and the agility in the deadlines and compliance with the operational requirements through the full systems life cycle.

The Instruction 58/2016, of October 28th, of the Secretary of State for Defense, by which the Spanish Ministry of Defense Communications and Information Systems Overarching Architecture (AG CIS/TIC) is aproved, establishes the principles to develop the CIS Architecture.

This includes: Standarized models for hierachical architectures, Standarized process for architectures development, Reuse and traceability of the architectures content, Service-oriented approach, Shared architectures information.

To that end, collaborative work systems will be used to facilitate the understanding of the relationships between capabilities, systems and CIS components in every level and between different architecture levels.

A general common repository will be created where the Spanish Ministry of Defense CIS Architectures will be stored once they are aproved, including the metadata which facilitates its location, record, classification, access, maintenance and provision.
This department level repository will facilitate the reuse and traceability of the content of all Architectures.
On the other hand, the aforementioned AG CIS/TIC includes, among its derived actions, the following steps for its development as follows.

Enable the incremental and sequential development of the Reference and Target CIS Architectures of the Spanish Ministry of Defense, in accordance with what it is established in the AG CIS/TIC and with the operative priorities of the Armed Forces (FAS), guaranteeing full ingration of the CIS Capabilities of the Department in the interoperability policy framework that ensures the end-to-end service provision.

Harmonize the process between the CIS Architecture development and the CIS resources and finance planning in the Defense Planning framework, ensuring the alignment of the CIS Capabilities with the Armed Forces (FAS) and the Department needs regarding the available financial resources.
This RFI focuses on the technical and functional characteristics of the architecture development tool and its support through the full life cycle.
